manufacturer_documents.device: Philips IntelliVue 6100/6300/6500 model family, release R.0 onwards only

parameters.name: Heart rhythm trace
parameters.explanation: Continuous 3-lead ECG monitoring allows early recognition and prompt treatment of life-threatening arrhythmias, and the monitoring must be supervised by someone skilled at interpreting and responding to changes (UKKA and Resuscitation Council UK, UK adults).

parameters.name: Heart rate
parameters.explanation: The displayed heart rate is an estimate calculated from the monitored signal. Compare it with the patient's pulse, perfusion and tracing; poor contact or artifact may produce misleading readings.

parameters.name: Oxygen saturation
parameters.explanation: Pulse oximeters can underestimate or overestimate saturation, especially when the reading is borderline; overestimation has been reported in people with dark skin, and probe placement matters (NICE CG103, citing an NHS England patient safety alert).

parameters.name: Alarm priority
parameters.explanation: The Philips IntelliVue 6100/6300/6500 quick guide for release R.0 onward describes three urgency levels, using different visual and audible indicators. Priority signals urgency, not a confirmed diagnosis. Assess the patient immediately if unstable; acknowledge only as authorised and resolve the cause. Other models and configurations may differ.

safety_concepts.text: Check the patient first when an alarm sounds; assess responsiveness, breathing and perfusion. If unstable, summon emergency help without waiting for tracing or electrode troubleshooting.

monitoring_concepts.text: Observe the rhythm and print a 6-second strip as the checklist describes; compare with the patient.
Check alarm limits and priority against the authorised patient-specific plan and the device instructions. Do not silence or change limits merely to reduce nuisance alarms.

Consider poor perfusion, skin temperature and pigmentation when assessing the reliability of an oxygen saturation reading. If the reading conflicts with the patient's condition, reassess promptly and arrange confirmatory assessment with the clinical team; do not delay emergency help.

escalation_concepts.text: Know the emergency rhythms and call for help per unit protocol; thresholds follow the resuscitation policy.
